questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of this guideline as stated in section 1.1 of ICH Q8(R2)?

options.A: To specify the list of process documents a marketed product must have ready for a GMP on-site inspection, and to set how inspectors score and grade deficiencies
options.B: To provide the suggested content for the 3.2.P.2 section of the CTD, presenting knowledge gained through the application of scientific approaches and quality risk management
options.C: To set the standard values and acceptable ranges of release specifications for each dosage form, for direct citation by national pharmacopoeias as legal limits
options.D: To prescribe the minimum number of batches and the sampling plan required for process validation, as a minimum regulatory requirement for applicants and authorities alike

questions.explanation: Section 1.1 states that this guideline describes the suggested contents for the 3.2.P.2 section of the ICH M4 CTD format, which is an opportunity to present the knowledge gained through the application of scientific approaches and quality risk management (see Q9) and which can be updated across the product lifecycle. It is not a GMP inspection checklist, not a standard for specification values, and does not prescribe a number of validation batches; none of these are in the purpose statement of Q8(R2).

questions.question: A company's drug product is still in the clinical research stage, and it asks whether it must prepare 3.2.P.2 under Q8(R2). According to section 1.2, which of the following is correct?

options.A: It applies strictly to the submission content for all clinical stages, and a full 3.2.P.2 section must be submitted from the first clinical phase
options.B: It is completely unrelated to the clinical stage, and the development team need not consider any of its principles during clinical development, referring to them only at the marketing application
options.C: Only biological products must follow this guideline during the clinical stage; chemical drugs and other types of products are always outside its applicability
options.D: It does not apply to submissions during the clinical research stage of drug development, but its principles are still worth considering in that stage

questions.explanation: Section 1.2 states explicitly that the guideline does not apply to submissions during the clinical research stage of drug development, but that its principles are important and should be considered during that stage; it also notes that the guideline might be appropriate for other types of products and that consultation with regulatory authorities can be sought. Therefore "fully mandatory" and "completely unrelated" are both wrong, and there is no distinction between biological and chemical drugs.

questions.question: Company A submits a large number of batch data but lacks a mechanistic understanding of the process; Company B has less data but clearly presents deep scientific knowledge of material attributes and process parameters. According to Q8(R2), what does the degree of regulatory flexibility mainly depend on?

options.A: The level of relevant scientific knowledge provided, not the volume of data, so Company B is more likely to obtain flexibility
options.B: The total number of batches and data submitted; the more data, the better quality is demonstrated, so Company A has the advantage in flexibility
options.C: The applicant's company size and the number of products previously marketed, which has no direct relationship to the knowledge demonstrated in this submission
options.D: Whether a similar product has already been approved; with a precedent, the same degree of regulatory flexibility is automatically applied without additional justification

questions.explanation: Both section 2 and section 1.1 state that the degree of regulatory flexibility depends on the level of relevant scientific knowledge provided, and stress that "the level of knowledge gained, and not the volume of data" is the basis for science-based submission and assessment. Data volume, company size, and precedent are not bases stated in the guideline.

questions.question: A product has an approved design space. The manufacturing department adjusts a process parameter from one point within the design space to another. Which of the following is consistent with Q8(R2)?

options.A: Even for parameter changes within the design space, an application must still be filed with the authority and approval obtained each time before implementation
options.B: The design space takes effect when declared by the manufacturer, without assessment and approval by the regulatory authority and without being subject to any change regulations
options.C: Working within the design space is not considered a change; moving out of the design space is considered a change and would normally initiate a regulatory post-approval change process
options.D: Moving out of the design space is still an internal process adjustment, and as long as the finished product passes testing it is not considered a change and need not be reported to the authority

questions.explanation: Section 2 states that the design space is proposed by the applicant and is subject to regulatory assessment and approval; working within the design space is not considered a change, whereas movement out of the design space is considered a change and would normally initiate a regulatory post-approval change process. Statements that every adjustment within the space requires an application, that no review is needed, or that moving out is still not a change are therefore all contrary to the text.

questions.question: According to section 2 of Q8(R2), a higher degree of product and process understanding demonstrated by the applicant can create more flexible regulatory approaches. Which of the following is NOT an example listed in the text?

options.A: Making process improvements within the approved design space without a further regulatory review process
options.B: Exempting all process changes from regulatory review, whether or not the change is within the design space
options.C: Reducing the number of post-approval submissions and facilitating risk-based regulatory decisions on review and inspection
options.D: Reducing end-product release testing through real-time quality control, as a way to lessen the testing burden

questions.explanation: The flexibilities listed in the text include risk-based regulatory decisions (review and inspection), process improvements within the approved design space without further review, reduction of post-approval submissions, and real-time quality control leading to reduced end-product release testing. There is no statement that all changes are exempt from review; changes outside the design space still initiate a post-approval change process.

questions.question: Which statement about the requirements in 2.1.1 for the properties of the drug substance is correct?

options.A: Physicochemical properties are independent of one another, so each need only be examined individually, without considering possible interrelationships and combined effects
options.B: Only solid-state properties deliberately designed into the drug substance need to be discussed; other naturally occurring properties can always be skipped in drug product development
options.C: Properties can be interrelated and may need to be considered in combination; the study results can be used to support the drug substance specification (3.2.S.4.5)
options.D: Drug substance properties relate only to the drug substance specification, and no drug product studies are needed to assess their impact on drug product performance and manufacturability

questions.explanation: Section 2.1.1 states that properties of the drug substance that can influence the performance of the drug product and its manufacturability, or that were specifically designed into the drug substance, should be identified and discussed; these properties can be interrelated and may need to be considered in combination, drug product studies can be conducted where necessary, and the results can be used to support the drug substance specification in 3.2.S.4.5. Therefore "independent of one another", "only designed properties", and "no drug product studies needed" are all inconsistent with the text.

questions.question: In describing excipients, what range of substances does Q8(R2) section 2.1.2 require to be covered?

options.A: All substances used in the manufacture of the drug product, whether or not they appear in the final product (such as processing aids)
options.B: Only the components listed in the final drug product formula; substances used during processing but ultimately removed need not be discussed
options.C: Only excipients that have a pharmacopoeial monograph; excipients without a monograph are outside the scope of this section
options.D: Only excipients with an activity-related function, such as antioxidants; fillers and diluents need not be discussed

questions.explanation: Section 2.1.2 states explicitly that the discussion should include all substances used in the manufacture of the drug product, whether or not they appear in the finished product (for example, processing aids), and that for each excipient the choice, concentration, and characteristics that can influence drug product performance should be discussed with reference to its function, together with demonstration that it achieves its intended function throughout the shelf life. Limiting the scope to "formula table only", "monograph only", or "specific functions only" is not what the text requires.

questions.question: The commercial formulation of a product differs slightly from the formulation used in the pivotal clinical batches. According to 2.2.1, how should the applicant handle this?

options.A: As long as the commercial formulation passes release testing, the difference from the clinical formulation need not be explained, because clinical batches are irrelevant to the submission
options.B: All clinical trials must be repeated, otherwise the commercial formulation cannot be used in the marketing application or serve as its basis
options.C: The commercial formulation need only be listed in the batch formula; an explanation of differences is internal information and need not be presented in the pharmaceutical development section
options.D: Clearly describe the differences and provide the rationale, and summarize comparative in vitro or in vivo studies that link the two formulations

questions.explanation: Section 2.2.1 requires a summary of the formulations used in clinical safety and efficacy studies and in any relevant bioavailability or bioequivalence studies; any changes between the commercial formulation and the pivotal clinical batches and primary stability batches must be clearly described and rationalized, and comparative in vitro (such as dissolution) or in vivo studies linking the two must be summarized, with study numbers cross-referenced. The text does not require repeating all clinical trials, nor does it allow omitting the explanation of differences.

questions.question: What is the position of Q8(R2) section 2.2.2 on overage in drug product manufacture?

options.A: Overage is encouraged to extend shelf life, as long as the final release testing is acceptable, with no further justification needed
options.B: It is generally discouraged; the amount, reason, and justification must be explained, and it must be included in the drug substance amount in the batch formula
options.C: Overage need not be justified as long as it does not appear in the final formulation, because it does not affect the drug substance content of the finished product
options.D: The amount of overage need only be noted in the internal batch record and need not be included in the drug substance amount in the submitted batch formula (3.2.P.3.2)

questions.explanation: Section 2.2.2 states that the use of overages of the drug substance to compensate for degradation during manufacture or shelf life, or to extend shelf life, is generally discouraged; any overage, whether or not it appears in the final product, must be justified with respect to safety and efficacy, including 1) the amount, 2) the reason (for example, documented expected manufacturing losses), and 3) justification of the amount, and it must be included in the drug substance amount in the batch formula in 3.2.P.3.2. Therefore "encouraged", "no need to explain if not in the finished product", and "not included in the batch formula" are all contrary to the text.

questions.topic: Physicochemical and biological properties of DP
questions.question: According to 2.2.3, which of the following types of information is appropriate for discussion in the section on "physicochemical and biological properties of the drug product"?

options.A: The basis for selecting dissolution rather than disintegration testing, and the development and suitability of the selected test
options.B: Audit reports on drug substance suppliers, supplier qualification procedures, and the content of quality agreement terms with suppliers
options.C: Batch release records for commercial batches, and summaries of investigations and corrective and preventive actions for deviations in individual batches
options.D: The validation plan for container closure integrity testing, and calibration records and periodic calibration arrangements for the test instrument

questions.explanation: Section 2.2.3 explains that the physicochemical and biological properties relevant to the safety, performance, or manufacturability of the drug product should be discussed, for example the development of respirable fraction testing for inhalation products; the basis for choosing a means of confirming release, such as dissolution or disintegration testing, and the development and suitability of the selected test can be placed in this section, with cross-reference to the stability data in 3.2.P.8.3. Supplier audits, batch release records, and integrity calibration documents do not belong in this section.

questions.question: The development team for a sterile injectable is writing the 2.3 manufacturing process development content. According to Q8(R2), which statement about the sterilization method is correct?

options.A: Terminal sterilization is always the method used; as long as the equipment is validated, no justification of the choice of method is needed
options.B: The sterilization method need only be chosen for the drug product itself; the primary packaging material is not within the scope of the sterilization method selection
options.C: The choice of sterilization method is something decided after commercial manufacture begins, and need not be discussed or justified during development
options.D: An appropriate sterilization method should be selected for the drug product and the primary packaging material, and the reason for the choice should be explained

questions.explanation: Section 2.3 provides that for products intended to be sterile, an appropriate method of sterilization should be chosen for the drug product and primary packaging material, and the choice should be justified. The text does not specify a fixed method, does not exclude the primary packaging material, and requires the explanation at the time of process development rather than after commercial manufacture begins.

questions.question: According to 2.3, when comparing significant differences between pivotal clinical/primary stability batches and the commercial process (3.2.P.3.3), which of the following is NOT information listed in the text?

options.A: Information such as the batch identification (for example, batch number) and its use (for example, bioequivalence study batch number)
options.B: The batch manufacturing site and the batch size, and other information useful for comparing the processes
options.C: The seniority, training hours, and qualification records of the operators who performed the batch
options.D: Any significant equipment differences, for example differences in design, operating principle, or size

questions.explanation: Section 2.3 states that the impact of the differences on performance, manufacturability, and quality must be discussed and presented in a way that facilitates comparison, with information such as: (1) batch identification and use, (2) manufacturing site, (3) batch size, and (4) significant equipment differences. Operator seniority and training hours are not among the listed items.

questions.question: A product is administered with a pen injection device. According to 2.4, container closure system, how should the applicant demonstrate this?

options.A: As long as the device material meets food-grade requirements and passes a general visual inspection, accurate dosing can be considered demonstrated
options.B: By demonstrating that the device delivers a reproducible and accurate dose under test conditions that simulate use as closely as possible
options.C: By testing once under ideal laboratory conditions, without simulating actual use, because the dosing device is ancillary packaging
options.D: The dosing device is packaging, so reproducibility of the dose need not be demonstrated; it is enough to confirm that the device is visually intact and clearly labelled

questions.explanation: Section 2.4 states that if a dosing device is used (such as a dropper, pen injection device, or dry powder inhaler), it should be demonstrated that a reproducible and accurate dose of the product is delivered under testing conditions that simulate use of the product as closely as possible. Material compliance, a single ideal test, or visual inspection alone is not sufficient to meet this requirement.

questions.question: A multi-dose product contains an antimicrobial preservative, and its specification tests only the preservative content (a chemical test). According to 2.5, microbiological attributes, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Antimicrobial effectiveness testing must show that the minimum specified concentration is effective, and the concentration used must be justified for effectiveness and safety
options.B: Testing the preservative content in the specification is enough to demonstrate preservative effectiveness, so no separate antimicrobial effectiveness testing is needed during development
options.C: It is enough to show that the maximum specified concentration is effective, since if the highest concentration is effective the lowest must necessarily be effective too and need not be verified
options.D: The preservative concentration should be as high as possible to ensure effectiveness throughout the shelf life, and its safety need not be considered separately during development

questions.explanation: Section 2.5 explains that the specification typically includes a chemical test for preservative content, but antimicrobial preservative effectiveness must still be demonstrated during development; antimicrobial effectiveness testing must show that the minimum specified concentration is effective, and the concentration used must be justified in terms of effectiveness and safety, using the minimum concentration that gives the required effectiveness throughout the shelf life. Where relevant, microbiological challenge testing that simulates patient use should also be performed.

questions.question: A lyophilized powder for injection must be reconstituted with a diluent and may be further diluted in a large-volume infusion bag. According to 2.6, what should the development data cover?

options.A: Only the shelf life of the product in its original package; compatibility with diluents is the hospital's responsibility and need not be discussed here
options.B: As long as the diluent meets pharmacopoeial specifications, compatibility issues such as precipitation or stability need not be assessed separately
options.C: Only a single concentration at room temperature need be assessed, without covering concentration extremes or specifying the recommended storage temperature
options.D: Compatibility with the diluent, in-use shelf life, storage temperature, and concentration extremes, to support the labeling

questions.explanation: Section 2.6 requires that the compatibility of the drug product with reconstitution diluents (for example, precipitation and stability) be addressed to provide appropriate and supporting information for the labeling; the content must cover the in-use shelf life at the recommended storage temperature and the possible concentration extremes. Mixing or diluting prior to administration (for example, adding to large-volume infusion bags) may also need to be addressed, so passing it to the hospital or looking at a single condition does not fit the text.

questions.question: According to the section 3 terminology of Q8(R2), what is the definition of Continuous Process Verification?

options.A: An alternative approach to process validation in which manufacturing process performance is continuously monitored and evaluated
options.B: The traditional validation approach of showing, once, with three consecutive successful batches that the process is validated, after which the process is fixed and no longer monitored
options.C: A one-time comparative study performed only after a process change, used to evaluate the extent of the change's impact on quality
options.D: Statistical trend analysis of the final product release test results only, without covering in-process monitoring and evaluation of process performance

questions.explanation: The glossary defines it as an alternative approach to process validation in which manufacturing process performance is continuously monitored and evaluated. A one-time demonstration with three batches is the traditional approach; a one-time study after a change and trend analysis of release results alone do not match the definition of continuously monitoring process performance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the definition of Design Space in the Part I glossary is most accurate?

options.A: The acceptable range of any process parameter obtained from one-variable experiments, usable once reviewed and approved by the manufacturer's internal quality unit
options.B: The multidimensional combination and interaction of input variables and process parameters that have been demonstrated to provide assurance of quality, proposed by the applicant and subject to regulatory approval
options.C: The range of operation commonly seen during normal operation of the process, which need not be shown experimentally to assure quality
options.D: A uniform operating range set by the regulatory authority and applicable to all similar products, which an applicant may not propose or modify on its own

questions.explanation: The glossary defines the design space as the "multidimensional combination and interaction" of input variables and process parameters that have been demonstrated to provide assurance of quality; it is proposed by the applicant and is subject to regulatory assessment and approval. A one-variable range, a commonly seen operating range, and a uniform authority range all lack either the "multidimensional interaction and demonstrated" element or the "proposed by the applicant" element.

questions.question: A plant uses near-infrared (NIR) to measure moisture content in real time during granulation and adjusts the operation according to the result to ensure final quality. Which term in the Q8(R2) glossary does this practice best match?

options.A: Formal Experimental Design: a structured method for determining the relationship between factors affecting a process and its output, also known as DoE
options.B: Process Robustness: the ability of a process to tolerate variability of materials and changes of the process and equipment without negative impact on quality, a property of the process
options.C: Process Analytical Technology (PAT): a system for designing, analyzing, and controlling manufacturing through timely in-process measurements
options.D: Lifecycle: all phases in the life of a product from the initial development through marketing until the product's discontinuation, covering the whole product life

questions.explanation: The glossary defines PAT as a system for designing, analyzing, and controlling manufacturing through timely (that is, during processing) measurements of critical quality and performance attributes of raw and in-process materials and processes, with the goal of ensuring final product quality; real-time NIR measurement with adjustment, as in the question, fits exactly. Formal Experimental Design is DoE, a structured method for determining the relationship between factors and output; Process Robustness and Lifecycle are separate concepts.

questions.question: A process maintains product quality unaffected despite variability between raw material batches and slight changes in equipment. According to the glossary, which concept does this describe?

options.A: Continuous Process Verification
options.B: Design Space (a demonstrated multidimensional combination of variables)
options.C: Formal Experimental Design
options.D: Process Robustness

questions.explanation: The glossary defines Process Robustness as the ability of a process to tolerate variability of materials and changes of the process and equipment without negative impact on quality. CPV is an alternative approach to validation based on continuously monitoring process performance; Design Space is a demonstrated multidimensional combination of variables; Formal Experimental Design is the DoE method and is not a description of process capability.

questions.question: Which pair of statements of the Part I glossary definitions is entirely correct?

options.A: Quality is the ideal state of a product being completely free of any impurities; Lifecycle refers only to the stages after the product is commercially marketed
options.B: Quality refers only to a product passing release testing; Lifecycle refers to the whole manufacturing operation from raw material purchase to finished product shipment
options.C: Quality is the suitability of a product for its intended use, including identity, strength, and purity; Lifecycle covers development, marketing, and discontinuation
options.D: Quality is an overall evaluation of a product's price and appearance; Lifecycle is the time a single batch takes from production to release

questions.explanation: The glossary: Quality is the suitability of either a drug substance or drug product for its intended use, including attributes such as identity, strength, and purity; Lifecycle is all phases in the life of a product from the initial development through marketing until the product's discontinuation. The other options narrow Quality to impurity-free or release-passing only, or reduce Lifecycle to a post-marketing stage, a manufacturing flow, or a single batch, none of which matches the definitions.

questions.question: A company is developing a sterile injectable. According to Annex 2.1 and 2.2, which statement is correct?

options.A: The QTPP is drawn up only after development ends, to summarize the characteristics of the final product, and does not affect design decisions during development
options.B: The QTPP is the basis of design for development; CQAs for an injectable can include sterility, and the list of potential CQAs can be revised as knowledge increases
options.C: CQAs relate only to the final drug product; the drug substance, excipients, and intermediates never have CQAs of their own
options.D: Once the list of potential CQAs is set early in development it is fixed and cannot be changed as process and product understanding increases

questions.explanation: Annex 2.1 states that the QTPP forms the basis of design for the development of the product; 2.2 states that CQAs are generally associated with the drug substance, excipients, intermediates, and drug product, that non-oral dosage forms can include product-specific aspects such as sterility for parenterals, and that the list of potential CQAs can be modified as the formulation and manufacturing process are selected and knowledge increases, and can be prioritized using quality risk management. Therefore "QTPP drawn up afterwards", "only the drug product has CQAs", and "fixed list" are all incorrect.

questions.topic: PAR vs design space and edge of failure
questions.question: A team has used one-variable experiments to establish proven acceptable ranges (PARs) for temperature, time, and water quantity separately, and wants to declare the combination of the three ranges directly as the design space. According to Annex 2.4.5 and 2.4.6, which of the following is correct?

options.A: The combination of PARs is the design space, because each individual parameter range has been shown to be acceptable, so no multivariate study is needed
options.B: The edge of failure and failure modes of every parameter must first be demonstrated, otherwise the design space cannot be established and will not be approved by the authority
options.C: PARs have no value at all; knowledge from one-variable experiments cannot be used for process understanding or for risk assessment
options.D: A combination of PARs does not constitute a design space, but still provides useful knowledge; determining the edge of failure is helpful but not essential

questions.explanation: Annex 2.4.5 states explicitly that "A combination of proven acceptable ranges does not constitute a design space", but PARs based on univariate experimentation can provide useful information about the process; 2.4.6 explains that determining the edge of failure or demonstrating failure modes can be helpful but is not an essential part of establishing a design space. The three incorrect options each contradict one of these two points.

questions.question: A product is shear sensitive in a mixing operation, and the applicant wants the design space to be usable across several scales. According to Annex 2.4.4, which approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Use scale-independent parameters, for example describing the design space by shear rate rather than by impeller speed
options.B: Describe the design space directly in terms of the impeller speed obtained from small-scale experiments, assuming it applies at any scale with no conversion needed
options.C: There is no need to explain how a small-scale or pilot-scale design space relates to commercial scale, or to discuss risks when scaling up operations
options.D: The design space can be established only at commercial scale; the guideline does not allow a design space to be developed at small or pilot scale or models to be used

questions.explanation: Annex 2.4.4 states that a design space can be developed at any scale, but the relevance of a small- or pilot-scale design space to the commercial scale must be justified and the risks of scale-up discussed; if the design space is to span multiple scales, it should be described in terms of relevant scale-independent parameters, for example shear rate rather than rotational speed when shear is a concern, and dimensionless numbers or scaling models can also be included. The other options say the opposite.

questions.question: Which statement about control strategy and real-time release testing (RTRT) in Annex 2.5 is correct?

options.A: RTRT can replace end-product testing and also completely exempts the batch review and QC release steps required by GMP
options.B: RTRT can replace end-product testing but does not replace the review and quality control steps called for under GMP to release the batch
options.C: The control strategy must adopt RTRT entirely as the only basis for release and cannot include any end-product testing elements
options.D: The control strategy includes only end-product specifications; control of material attributes and control of unit operations are not covered by the control strategy

questions.explanation: Annex 2.5 explains that RTRT can replace end-product testing but "does not replace the review and quality control steps called for under GMP to release the batch"; a control strategy can include different elements (for example, one relying on end-product testing and another on RTRT), the rationale for the alternative approach must be explained, and it can include controls on input material attributes, specifications, unit operations, and so on. The three incorrect options each contradict these statements.

questions.question: A design space is represented by a mathematical model. According to Annex 2.6, which statement is correct?

options.A: Any model maintenance activity must first obtain regulatory approval, including routine maintenance and confirmation that does not alter the design space at all
options.B: Once approved, a design space cannot be changed, and may not be expanded or reduced even if additional process knowledge is gained later
options.C: When the design space is unchanged, model maintenance can be managed under the company's internal quality system; changing the design space is subject to regional regulatory requirements
options.D: Changes to the design space are decided entirely by the company, without being subject to any regional regulatory requirements and without notifying the authority

questions.explanation: Annex 2.6 states that process performance can be monitored and trended; for a design space that uses a mathematical model, periodic maintenance helps ensure model performance, and where the design space is not changed this is an activity that can be managed within the company's internal quality system; after more knowledge is gained, a company may wish to expand, reduce, or redefine the design space, but changes must follow regional regulatory requirements.

questions.question: A process parameter has been shown in experiments to have no impact on any CQA when varied. According to the Part II glossary, how should this parameter be classified?

options.A: It is not a CPP, because the definition of a CPP requires that its variability have an impact on a CQA
options.B: It is still a CPP, because the guideline requires all process parameters to be considered critical and to be monitored and controlled
options.C: It is a CPP, because any parameter included in the design space automatically becomes a critical process parameter that needs to be controlled
options.D: It is a CQA, because any process parameter that can be measured is a critical quality attribute, without separately evaluating its impact on quality

questions.explanation: The glossary defines a CPP as a process parameter whose variability has an impact on a CQA and therefore should be monitored or controlled to ensure the process produces the desired quality. If it is shown to have no impact on a CQA, it does not meet the CPP definition. A CQA is a physical, chemical, biological, or microbiological property of the product, not a process parameter; the three incorrect options confuse these concepts.

questions.question: According to the Part II glossary, what does the definition of Quality by Design (QbD) emphasize?

options.A: A development and management approach relying mainly on end-product test results, repeating testing until the product passes
options.B: Relying on empirical experiments that change one variable at a time, drawing conclusions and setting process conditions after accumulating enough batches
options.C: A systematic approach to development that begins with predefined objectives and emphasizes product and process understanding and control, based on sound science and quality risk management
options.D: A method used only at the validation stage, with no need to set predefined objectives or perform risk assessment and management during development

questions.explanation: The glossary: QbD is a systematic approach to development that begins with predefined objectives and emphasizes product and process understanding and process control, based on sound science and quality risk management. Reliance on end-product testing and one-variable-at-a-time empirical experiments are features of the minimal approach described in Appendix 1; QbD is also not used only at the validation stage.

questions.question: According to Appendix 1, which of the following is a feature of the "enhanced QbD approach" rather than the "minimal approach"?

options.A: A fixed process, with validation primarily based on initial full-scale batches and reactive lifecycle management (problem solving and corrective action)
options.B: In-process tests used mainly as go/no go decisions, with off-line analysis as the main means of testing
options.C: The drug product specification as the primary means of control, with specifications based on batch data available at the time of registration
options.D: A process adjustable within the design space, with lifecycle validation ideally combined with CPV, and preventive actions that facilitate continual improvement

questions.explanation: In the Appendix 1 comparison table, the minimal approach is characterized by a fixed process, validation based primarily on initial full-scale batches, in-process tests mainly as go/no go, off-line analysis, a specification as the primary control based on batch data at the time of registration, and reactive lifecycle management. The enhanced approach has an adjustable process within the design space, lifecycle validation with CPV where possible, preventive action, and facilitation of continual improvement. The text also notes that establishing a design space or RTRT is not necessarily expected in the enhanced approach.

questions.question: According to the example in Appendix 2A, how does a cross-functional team use risk assessment tools to identify the variables that should be studied first?

options.A: First list the variables in a fishbone diagram, then rank them with FMEA by probability, severity, and detectability, and finally evaluate the highly ranked variables with DoE
options.B: First test all variables to the same extent with a design of experiments, then record the results in a fishbone diagram and directly set the final specification
options.C: The quality department alone lists the variables from experience, with no cross-functional team and no ranking tool or experimental confirmation needed
options.D: Rank variables with FMEA on severity alone, then directly set the specification and control strategy after ranking, with no further experiments

questions.explanation: Appendix 2A: a cross-functional team of experts first develops an Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram to identify variables that might impact the quality attribute of interest, then ranks them by probability, severity, and detectability using FMEA or a similar tool, based on prior knowledge and initial experimental data; the highly ranked variables are then evaluated with DoE and similar methods to gain further understanding and to establish a control strategy. The sequence, personnel, or criteria in the other options do not match.

questions.question: Appendix 2B uses the effect of a granule drying operation (initial moisture content, temperature, mean particle size) on degradation product Y as an example. According to the example, which conclusion is correct?

options.A: There is no interaction between any pair of the three parameters, so each parameter's range can be set independently without considering the others
options.B: There is an interaction between every pair of the three parameters, and the lines in all pairwise plots are non-parallel with different slopes
options.C: Only temperature and mean particle size interact; initial moisture content is independent of the other two parameters
options.D: Initial moisture content and temperature interact while the other pairs do not; this can be judged from the relative slopes of the lines or curves

questions.explanation: Appendix 2B explains that the relative slopes of the lines or curves in the plots show whether there is an interaction; in the example, initial moisture content and temperature interact, while there is no interaction between initial moisture content and mean particle size or between temperature and mean particle size. Therefore "all independent", "all interacting", and "only temperature and particle size" are inconsistent with the example.
